description: Figure 8 presents three pie charts, each depicting the distribution of problem correctness across three difficulty levels—easy, medium, and hard—under two settings: with knowledge (w/ KNOWLEDGE) and without knowledge (w/o KNOWLEDGE), using the ZERO-SHOT method. Each chart is divided into four colored segments, corresponding to the categories N+K+, N-K+, N-K-, and N+K-, as indicated by the legend. The “easy” chart shows 55.4% for N+K+ (teal), 38.3% for N-K+ (yellow), and 4.6% for N-K- (red), with no percentage shown for N+K-. The “medium” chart displays 58.8% for N+K+ (teal), 35.4% for N-K+ (yellow), and 4.8% for N-K- (red), with no percentage shown for N+K-. The “hard” chart shows 37.3% for N+K+ (teal), 37.9% for N-K+ (orange), 6.7% for N-K- (red), and 18.1% for N+K- (light yellow). All charts are labeled with their respective difficulty level and the term “Zero-Shot” below them. The legend is positioned to the right of the charts, providing a color key for the four categories. The charts are arranged horizontally, with the “easy” chart on the left, the “medium” in the center, and the “hard” on the right.
